page_title: Understanding Modern Storage APIs:  A systematic study of libaio, SPDK, and io_uring

sources.entry: Understanding Modern Storage APIs: A systematic study of libaio, SPDK, and io_uring - Measures io_uring's polling modes against libaio and SPDK, and shows the kernel poller needs its own core.

summary.title: Understanding Modern Storage APIs: A systematic study of libaio, SPDK, and io_uring
summary.one_liner: io_uring's kernel-polling mode can approach SPDK's NVMe performance, but only with roughly twice as many CPU cores as drives, and it collapses when cores are scarce.
keywords: is io_uring as fast as spdk
takeaways: io_uring with kernel submission polling can reach within about 10% of SPDK's IOPS, since it removes system calls from the I/O path, but it needs about two cores per drive.
With too few cores, io_uring kernel polling degrades sharply: on one core it delivered about 13 KIOPS, and with 5 drives and no extra cores its throughput fell below half of libaio's.
Polling design matters more than the API alone: io_uring's completion polling (iou+p) matches SPDK only at low-to-medium throughput because system call overhead limits it at high queue depths.
SPDK gives the best performance in every configuration tested, but it lacks file system integration and kernel services such as access control, QoS and scheduling.
The authors recommend a hybrid, scale-aware choice of API and parameters based on core count and drive count, as their benchmark used fio on 20 Intel DC P3600 NVMe SSDs.
summary.summary: The paper is a systematic SYSTOR '22 study comparing Linux libaio, SPDK and io_uring on NVMe SSDs using fio with random 4KiB unbuffered reads. It tests io_uring in three modes: default interrupt-driven completion, completion polling (hipri), and a kernel submission-polling thread (sqthread_poll). Experiments vary queue depth, CPU cores per drive, and the number of drives up to 20 on a 20-core machine. The authors conclude with design guidelines for I/O-intensive applications, centred on the trade-offs of polling and core provisioning.
